quotes.text: Let us look stedfastly to the blood of Christ, and see how precious that blood is to God, which, having been shed for our salvation, has set the grace of repentance before the whole world.
quotes.author: Clement of Rome
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: If, then, the Father of all wished His Christ for the whole human family to take upon Him the curses of all, knowing that, after He had been crucified and was dead, He would raise Him up, why do you argue about Him, who submitted to suffer these things according to the Father's will, as if He were accursed, and do not rather bewail yourselves?
quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: ... because all were under penalty of the corruption of death He gave it over to death in the stead of all, and offered it to the Father ...
quotes.author: Athanasius
quotes.work: On the Incarnation of the Word
quotes.edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), series 2, vol. 4
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: "That by the grace of God He should taste death for every man," not for the faithful only, but even for the whole world: for He indeed died for all; But what if all have not believed? He hath fulfilled His own [part].
quotes.author: John Chrysostom
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: Christ the Lord, also, Who died for all, will grieve that the price of His blood was paid in vain.
quotes.author: Ambrose
quotes.work: On the Duties of the Clergy
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: Ignorance thou mayest not plead, for to this end He came down, that thou mayest believe; if thou believest not, He has not come down for thee, has not suffered for thee.
quotes.author: Ambrose
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: ... in order that he that liveth, no longer for himself may live, but for Him that for all men hath died.
quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: This thy Bridegroom possesses the whole, because He purchased the whole. See at what price He purchased it, that thou mayest understand what He has purchased. What price has He given? He gave His blood.
quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: God no doubt wishes all men to be saved and to come into the knowledge of the truth; but yet not so as to take away from them free will, for the good or the evil use of which they may be most righteously judged.
quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.work: On the Spirit and the Letter
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: Accordingly, when we hear and read in Scripture that He "will have all men to be saved," although we know well that all men are not saved, we are not on that account to restrict the omnipotence of God, but are rather to understand the Scripture, "Who will have all men to be saved," as meaning that no man is saved unless God wills his salvation: not that there is no man whose salvation He does not will, but that no man is saved apart from His will ...
quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: ... but that we are to understand by "all men," the human race in all its varieties of rank and circumstances ...
quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: "He wills all men to be saved," is so said that all the predestinated may be understood by it, because every kind of men is among them.
quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: For there is a world whereof it is written, "That we might not be condemned with this world." For that world He prayeth not, for He is fully aware to what it is predestinated. And there is a world whereof it is written, "For the Son of man came not to condemn the world, but that the world through Him might be saved;" and hence the apostle also says, "God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself."
quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: At length theological questions came into the hands of the Schoolmen, who, although they were fruitful artificers of disputes, yet were unwilling to renew this subject. To them it seemed sufficient to teach that Christ died for all sufficiently, for the predestinated effectually ...
quotes.author: John Davenant
quotes.work: A Dissertation on the Death of Christ
quotes.edition: In his Exposition of Colossians, vol. 2, translated by Josiah Allport (London, 1832)

quotes.text: Since, then, Christ's Passion was a sufficient and a superabundant atonement for the sin and the debt of the human race, it was as a price at the cost of which we were freed from both obligations.
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: As stated above, since Christ's Passion preceded, as a kind of universal cause of the forgiveness of sins, it needs to be applied to each individual for the cleansing of personal sins.
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas
quotes.loc: part III, question 49, article 1, reply to objection 4
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: As Christ's Passion benefits all, for the forgiveness of sin and the attaining of grace and glory, whereas it produces no effect except in those who are united with Christ's Passion through faith and charity ...
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas
quotes.loc: part III, question 79, article 7, reply to objection 2
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: Hence it may be said of a just judge, that antecedently he wills all men to live; but consequently wills the murderer to be hanged. In the same way God antecedently wills all men to be saved, but consequently wills some to be damned, as His justice exacts.
quotes.author: Thomas Aquinas
quotes.loc: part I, question 19, article 6, reply to objection 1
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: And although God knows who are his, and now and then mention is made of the small number of the elect, yet we must hope well of all, and not rashly judge any man to be a reprobate ...
quotes.author: Second Helvetic Confession (1566, written by Heinrich Bullinger)
quotes.edition: Philip Schaff, Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: ... That all the time he lived on earth, but especially at the end of his life, he bore, in body and soul, the wrath of God against the sin of the whole human race, in order that by his passion, as the only atoning sacrifice, he might redeem our body and soul from everlasting damnation, and obtain for us the grace of God, righteousness, and eternal life.
quotes.author: Heidelberg Catechism (1563)
quotes.edition: Philip Schaff, Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: ... Therefore, as he died for all, in respect to the sufficiency of his ransom ; -and for the faithful alone in respect to the efficacy of the same, so also he willed to die for all in general, as touching the sufficiency of his merit ...
quotes.author: Zacharias Ursinus

quotes.text: But he willed to die for the elect alone as touching the efficacy of his death, that is, he would not only sufficiently merit grace and life for them alone, but also effectually confers these upon them, grants faith, and the holy Spirit ...
quotes.author: Zacharias Ursinus
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (matched to a scanned page; small scan errors possible)

quotes.text: ... he shows himself to be reconciled to the whole world, when he invites all men without exception to the faith of Christ, which is nothing else than an entrance into life.
quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: And he has employed the universal term whosoever, both to invite all indiscriminately to partake of life, and to cut off every excuse from unbelievers.
quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: He makes this favor common to all, because it is propounded to all, and not because it is in reality extended to all; for though Christ suffered for the sins of the whole world, and is offered through God's benignity indiscriminately to all, yet all do not receive him.
quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: By the word many he means not a part of the world only, but the whole human race; for he contrasts many with one; as if he had said, that he will not be the Redeemer of one man only, but will die in order to deliver many from the condemnation of the curse.
quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.work: Harmony of the Gospels, on Mark 14:24 (with Matthew 26:28)
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: He openly declares that he does not pray for the world, because he has no solicitude but about his own flock, which he received from the hand of the Father.
quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: ... the Apostle simply means, that there is no people and no rank in the world that is excluded from salvation; because God wishes that the gospel should be proclaimed to all without exception.
quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: They who seek to avoid this absurdity, have said that Christ suffered sufficiently for the whole world, but efficiently only for the elect. This solution has commonly prevailed in the schools. Though then I allow that what has been said is true, yet I deny that it is suitable to this passage; for the design of John was no other than to make this benefit common to the whole Church.
quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.draft_tag: VERIFIED (exact match to the public-domain text)

quotes.text: That Christ died for all men, and, as the Lamb of God, took away the sins of the whole world.
quotes.author: Saxon Visitation Articles (1592, Lutheran)

quotes.text: Jesus Christ, the Saviour of the world, died for all men and for every man, so that he has obtained for them all, by his death on the cross, redemption and the forgiveness of sins; yet that no one actually enjoys this forgiveness of sins ...
quotes.author: The Remonstrants
quotes.edition: Philip Schaff, Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3

quotes.text: The death of the Son of God is the only and most perfect sacrifice and satisfaction for sin; is of infinite worth and value, abundantly sufficient to expiate the sins of the whole world.

quotes.edition: Philip Schaff, Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3 (older English text)

quotes.text: Moreover the promise of the gospel is, that whosoever believeth in Christ crucified shall not perish, but have everlasting life. This promise, together with the command to repent and believe, ought to be declared and published to all nations, and to all persons promiscuously and without distinction, to whom God out of his good pleasure sends the gospel.
quotes.author: Synod of Dort
quotes.edition: Philip Schaff, Creeds of Christendom, vol. 3

quotes.text: ... this is not owing to any defect or insufficiency in the sacrifice offered by Christ upon the cross, but is wholly to be imputed to themselves.

quotes.text: ... it was the will of God, that Christ by the blood of the cross, whereby he confirmed the new covenant, should effectually redeem out of every people, tribe, nation, and language, all those, and those only, who were from eternity chosen to salvation, and given to him by the Father ...

quotes.work: A Dissertation on the Death of Christ
